findings.claim: There is NO pedagogy record for elf-b16-003 in this round. reviews/pedagogy.jsonl covers only 6 of the batch's 7 units; elf-b16-003 is the one it misses, and the option set that a pedagogy MAJOR forced to be rewritten was therefore never re-reviewed by the pedagogy stage.
findings.evidence: reviews/pedagogy.jsonl has 8 lines but only 6 distinct candidate_ids: line 1 and line 6 are byte-identical ({"candidate_id":"elf-b16-004","stage":"pedagogy","verdict":"SOUND","reviewed_by":"pedagogy-review/opus","date":"2026-08-26"}) and line 4 and line 7 are byte-identical for las-b16-003. `grep -c elf-b16-003 reviews/pedagogy.jsonl` = 0. By contrast reviews-round1/pedagogy.jsonl carries all seven ids including 'elf-b16-003 pedagogy MINOR_FIXES', and this round's reviews/language.jsonl and reviews/integrated.jsonl both carry an elf-b16-003 line. The unit's own generator_meta.repair_log confirms the gap from the other side: rounds recorded are 2 (repair-agent), 3 (language-review/opus), 4 (integrated-review/opus) — no pedagogy round. The round-2 ticket is explicitly 'V-FINAL round-1 REFUTED. MAJOR (pedagogy)' and its remedy rewrote three of the four option texts (A, B and C all changed).
findings.why: The unit was refuted in round 1 on a PEDAGOGY major (blind-answerability), and the repair was a wholesale distractor rewrite — precisely the material whose blind-answerability only the pedagogy stage adjudicates. No pedagogy verdict exists for the rewritten option set, so the unit cannot be reported as pedagogy-cleared. The duplicate lines show this is a dispatch/write defect (two reviewers landed on the same id) rather than a deliberate skip, so nothing in the record documents the omission either. Fix: run pedagogy-review over candidates-final/elf-b16-003.json as it now stands and append the verdict before V-FINAL.

findings.claim: The rationale's blind-heuristic audit — the section the round-2 repair added specifically to close the blind-tell major, and which now claims 'Blind heuristics, all three audited' — does not establish its own conclusion for strip-the-absolutes. Applied in its ordinary student form (strike options that make a categorical claim), the heuristic strikes A, B and C and leaves the key D as the sole survivor.
findings.evidence: Rationale: "(2) Hedge and absolute: the key is a flat causal assertion with no hedge; the only hedged option ('usually', C) is wrong and the only absolutiser ('Every', A) is wrong, so neither 'pick the qualified answer' nor 'strip the absolutes' locates the key." But the current option texts read: A 'Every joint above the opening is running...' (Every); B 'The wind is still driving the rain into the brick, so nothing has reached the tray yet.' (nothing); C 'Nothing comes out of them while the wind blows, which usually means a missing stop end.' (Nothing); D 'Whatever the tray has caught stays on it, because the wind presses in at those joints.' — the only option carrying no categorical flag word. Three distractors make a categorical claim; the key does not. The mechanical gate cannot see this: gates/scripts/mech.py `_ABSOLUTIZERS` contains 'none' but NOT 'nothing', and I verified per-option with mech._has_absolutizer — A True, B False, C False, D False — so M-FORM passes (verified: gate_form -> pass) and generator_meta.hedge_balance_note's 'only one of the three distractors carries an absolutiser' is true only under that token list. This configuration is unchanged from round 1 (round-1 B '...so nothing has reached the tray yet.', round-1 C 'Nothing comes out of them, ...') and has now survived four rounds and two audits unexamined.
findings.why: This is the same failure class that refuted the unit in round 1 (a surface route to D that needs no passage), on a different axis, and it is asserted away in student-facing text rather than audited. The strongest counter-argument — that D's 'Whatever the tray has caught' is itself a universal — is exactly the analysis the rationale owes and does not give; a solver applying the flag-word form of the heuristic never reaches it. Because there is no pedagogy verdict for this round (see the blocker above), nothing in the record has weighed it. Fix is cheap and key-preserving: soften one distractor's categorical form (e.g. B '...so little has reached the tray yet.') so the key is not the sole uncategorical option, and state the 'Whatever' analysis in heuristic (2).

findings.claim: The trap label for A mis-scopes its cited quotation across the passage's own time division, and puts the rationale in tension with its own paragraph on C. 'Not all of the joints run, and none for long' is a LULL-phase statement, but it is used to diagnose an option that speaks about the pre-drop window.
findings.evidence: Passage order: 'While the wind is still on the wall, it pushes in at those same joints, and the tray holds what it has collected. In the lull, the tray lets go. Not all of the joints run, and none for long.' — the 'Not all' sentence follows 'In the lull' and describes the discharge in the lull. The stem's window is 'before the wind drops'. Rationale on A: 'A = quantifier upgrade welded to a reversed wind role. It absolutises the passage's own limit - "Not all of the joints run, and none for long" - into "Every joint ... is running"'. Read in the stem's window, 'not all run' entails that SOME run, which is contradicted by the rationale's own paragraph on C: 'Its first clause is exactly right - nothing does come out of the joints while the wind blows'. In the window the item actually tests, A's count error is zero-vs-every, not not-all-vs-every. generator_meta.engineered_traps and the round-2 repair note ('The quantifier_upgrade trap is preserved intact') carry the same mis-scoping.
findings.why: Integrated review's own criteria are that trap labels name the actual trap and that the rationale not contradict itself — the identical defect it correctly fixed for B in round 2 ('reversed sequence' -> 'premature stage / lag'). A student who takes the quantifier label at face value learns that some joints run during the storm, which is the opposite of what the key teaches. Not key-breaking: A is still false, and the rationale's primary named error for A (the reversed wind direction) is correct and sufficient. Fix is a scope clause: note that 'Not all of the joints run' describes the lull, and that in the stem's window the passage licenses no running joint at all.

findings.claim: The language stage's not_done disposition of the live G-REGISTER major rests on a factual premise about available fixes that the batch's own convention contradicts.
findings.evidence:
Round-3 not_done: 'Any real fix is a passage rewrite that would invalidate the physics verification and every declared statistic, so it stays with adjudication.' The live G-REGISTER finding (verdicts/verdicts-gregister.jsonl, severity major) is that the text 'stacks window head / cavity / tray / stop end / outer skin unglossed'. But the same batch glosses technical vocabulary by APPENDING a gloss line after the byline without touching a single existing sentence — elf-b16-001's passage ends '...
- Rhodri Kettlestrand, staff writer

veraison = the point in the season when grapes change colour and begin to ripen in earnest
glycoside = a compound formed when a sugar is joined chemically to another molecule' (same convention in elf-b15-001). A 'stop end = ...' line here would touch no mechanism sentence and invalidate no physics claim; it would only require re-declaring passage-length stats, which the unit already does for fk_grade under _band_deviation_declared.
findings.why: The disposition may still be the right call on genre grounds — the gate itself said 'Sits at the edge of the exemplar genre range rather than outside it' — but it is recorded on a false premise about cost, which is what a later adjudicator will read. The verdict CORRECTED is not overturned; the reasoning behind the one live major it hands on is. Fix: restate the disposition on genre grounds alone, or take the in-batch gloss-append route for 'stop end'.
